memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Those presenting an offering of silver or bronze brought it as an offering to the Lord, and everyone who had acacia wood for any part of the work brought it." - Exod 35:24 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Silver. Bronze. Wood. The value drops sharply as the verse goes on, and God receives all of it equally.

Somebody arrived with silver. Somebody else could only bring a few planks of acacia wood they had carried out of Egypt. Both offerings went into the same tabernacle. Both were named in the same sentence of Scripture.

This should settle something in us. God is not running a comparison. He never asked the wood-bringer why he had not brought silver.

"Everyone who had acacia wood" — that is the key phrase. Not everyone who wished they had gold. The people brought what they actually possessed.

We waste enormous energy on the offering we cannot make. If only I had more money, more time, more ability, more confidence — then I could really serve God. Meanwhile the wood sits in the corner.

Jesus praised the servant who was faithful with a few things (Matt 25:21), and He told a woman with an alabaster jar, "She did what she could" (Mark 14:8). That is the standard. Not what someone else could do. What you could.

Bring the wood. God is building with it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What do you actually have, rather than what do you wish you had?
2. Do you compare your capacity with others' and then give nothing?
3. What "small" thing could you offer God this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I stop wishing I had more to give. Here is what I have — please use it. Amen.
